links.outcome: LLM reasoning errors and association with guideline-discordant recommendations on oncology notes
links.effect: GPT-4 produced reasoning errors in 23.1% of note interpretations; errors were strongly associated with guideline-discordant recommendations and lower clinician-rated impact scores.
links.quote: GPT-4 produced reasoning errors in 23.1% of note interpretations, the majority reflecting cognitive bias patterns.

links.outcome: Whether endpoint accuracy masks reasoning failures in LLM oncology note interpretation
links.effect: Endpoint accuracy alone may mask clinically meaningful reasoning failures; GPT-5.1 had reduced error rates but retained structured failure patterns.
links.quote: Endpoint accuracy alone may mask clinically meaningful reasoning failures.

unlisted_practices: Taxonomy-based reasoning error evaluation of LLM outputs
LLM-based automated evaluators for detecting reasoning errors
Self-mitigation prompting to reduce reasoning errors

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating LLM reasoning failures on clinical oncology notes, testing automated LLM-based error detection and self-mitigation guardrails.

primary.practice: automated error detection and self-mitigation strategy
